correctness.rationale: The uniform atom estimate follows by separating one positive-mass atom and applying geometric-sum bounds and dominated convergence on its complement. An invertible weighted Vandermonde matrix cancels every finite set of residuals; independent block-length choices enforce both summable square norms and uniform control over all partial block sums. Ordinary coefficientwise limits therefore equal zero for each coordinate. Ransford 2026-10-10 Theorem 2.1/Lemma 3.2 apply under Re phi >= 1/2 and b outer, forcing trivial intersection with H(b). Polynomial triangular inversion and density show the entire product graph closure. No finite search is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result changes a one-function failure example into a complete severe-ill-posedness theorem for a natural broad family: not only is the phantom kernel dense with arbitrary finite prescribed Taylor jets, but any desired pair of input/output limits can arise from one graph-approximating sequence. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary atom accumulation, arbitrary masses, and any extra nonatomic part; the distinction between formal and canonical closed realizations is essential for de Branges–Rovnyak coefficient norm testing. This is a motivated structural boundary result and not a routine numerical or parameter substitution.
